title: The Fifteenth Constable: The Gold Thread of the Tailor
full_text:
The Fifteenth Constable related:

'A royal velvet cloak embroidered with gold was stolen from an emir’s carriage. A week later, a foreign merchant wore a plain black velvet coat in the bazaar, claiming it was bought in Aleppo.

I examined the hem: the gold embroidery had been ripped away, but inside the lining seam remained a single thread of distinctive crimson-and-gold twisted silk, woven with the secret knot used only by the master embroiderer of the Cairo Citadel!

The embroiderer confirmed his knot, the merchant confessed he had purchased the coat from a known receiver of stolen goods, and the burglary ring was dismantled, proving that the master’s stitch leaves an indelible signature.'
moral: Distinctive craftsmanship identifies stolen property that has been altered to deceive.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Fifteenth Constable's History"?

Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
